package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious package is described in this report. The article discusses general trends and concerns in software supply chain security, referencing real-world incidents (e.g., CircleCI, 3CX, IconBurst) and the prevalence of malicious code, secrets exposure, and tampering in open-source and third-party software.

behavioral_signatures: Malicious code injection into open-source or third-party packages
Secrets exfiltration during build or runtime
Software tampering (modification of legitimate code or binaries)
Unusual network communications from build or CI/CD environments
Unexpected data harvesting or credential access in package code
file_indicators: Unexpected changes in package.json, setup.py, or other manifest files
Presence of obfuscated or minified code in open-source modules
Suspicious scripts in .github/workflows or CI/CD configuration files
network_indicators: Outbound connections to unknown or suspicious domains during install/import
HTTP/S POST requests to webhook or data collection endpoints
Connections to external APIs not documented in package usage
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected or unauthorized code execution during package installation, import, or CI/CD pipeline runs. Flag packages that access sensitive files (e.g., credentials, SSH keys) or environment variables and attempt to exfiltrate data over the network. Use binary and behavioral analysis to detect tampering or the presence of malware, especially in open-source and third-party dependencies. Track changes to critical files and watch for obfuscated or undocumented code in package repositories.
